# Libby Titus

Libby Titus — **Libby Fagen** in the corpus, born Elizabeth Jurist, the
songwriter who wrote *"Love Has No Pride"* with Eric Kaz and who was married to
Donald Fagen of Steely Dan for thirty-one years — employed
[[wiki/people/annie-ulmer|Annie]] as a paid personal assistant in Manhattan
through the first half of **2024**. She was terminally ill for most of it. She
died on **13 October 2024, aged 77**, with an unpaid-wages dispute between them
still open.

Dan never met her. She exists in this corpus entirely through Annie's running
commentary — 116 messages — and she is the best-documented thing about Annie's
working life anywhere in the archive.

She matters here for four reasons, none of them about her. She is the **largest
documented income source on Annie's side** of the relationship; she **falsifies a
standing claim** this wiki carried about Annie's employment; the dispute that
ended the arrangement is the corpus's clearest instance of
[[wiki/mind/concepts/forensic-method|Dan's forensic register]] pointed outward on
somebody else's behalf; and her death removes that income five months before
Annie's documented collapse begins.

> **Sensitivity note.** This page concerns a named, identifiable person's final
> illness, her household finances and a wage dispute with her estate's
> predecessor, recorded from one side of a private conversation she was not party
> to and cannot correct. She has surviving family. It is kept because it is
> load-bearing for the biography this wiki is about, and written to that standard
> and no further. **It remains a candidate for the portal seal**
> (`wiki.locks.json`, portal repo); the operator's decision, still outstanding.

## The identification, now closed

> **GAP CLOSED [2026-08-23].** The first version of this page carried the
> identification as **inferred**, on two supports: Dan's own contemporaneous
> Tumblr link (`girlfriend-muse-libby-titus-elizabeth-jurist`, sent 2024-03-17,
> six hours after Annie's *"Did you know Libby was in a movie with Jack
> Nicholson"*), and a household **Donald** who claimed to be *"the first person to
> ever use the term 'gaslighting' in a song"* — Steely Dan's *Gaslighting Abbie* —
> at which *"Libby screamed 'YEAH ABOUT ME YOU ASSHOLE!'"* (2024-05-28).
>
> **Operator testimony of 2026-08-23 confirms it**, and adds the outcome: she is
> Libby Titus, she was married to Donald Fagen, and she has since died of the
> cancer the messages record. Filed at
> [[raw/people/captures/2026-08-23_libby-titus-identification-confirmed]].

> **CORRECTED [2026-08-23] — and the error is instructive.** That first version
> stated *"No message names her surname."* **False.** On 2024-08-14 Annie writes
> *"I also added in that draft that the hourly rate was set by **Libby Fagen**"*,
> and on 2024-08-08, *"Aka where Libby and Donald live lol."* The married name was
> in the corpus in plain text.
>
> The failure mode is the one `LLM_HANDOFF.md` already documents from the ENTP-T
> pass, and it has now happened twice: **a check scoped by the claim it is testing
> cannot disconfirm it.** The search was for `Titus`, because `Titus` was the
> hypothesis. The corpus says `Fagen`.

**The corpus also holds the death independently.** Dan writes ***"Libby died"***
on **2024-10-16**, and on **2024-11-01** pastes
`https://www.steelydan.com/news/libby-titus-fagen` — the Steely Dan announcement.
Public reporting gives 13 October 2024, three days before Dan's message. Treat
the date as secondary-sourced and corpus-corroborated; the *fact* is T0 and
primary both.

## The arc, February to October 2024

The work is bounded much more tightly than the mention count suggests: **112 of
the 116 messages fall between February and mid-August 2024.** Everything after is
aftermath.

**February — the trial.** It opens on **2024-02-08** with *"Libby asked me to come
again tomorrow lol"*, implying a prior visit the corpus does not hold. The
register is set immediately and never changes: the work and the money arrive in
the same sentence. *"I am taking Libby food from Antonuccis. So hopefully she will
give me something for bringing her food"* (02-11). *"I gotta gotta gotta get up
early tomorrow and help Libby. I need money."* (02-16).

**March — the illness, and the job turning medical.** On **2024-03-05** Annie
reports that Libby has told her she has brain cancer, and *"Libby just said 'I
think I'm dying..'"*; the next day, that it is also back in her right lung. From
there Annie is driving her to appointments, sitting through them (*"we are waiting
to see doctor now"*, 03-11), taking her for blood tests before a scheduled
procedure (03-17), and spending half-hours on the phone with doctors between
shifts (03-19). On **03-20** Libby emails her **cemetery plots**.

**May to July — the peak, and the second job.** The volume is highest in May
(25 mentions) and July (29). Annie is working both jobs — *"Now I'll be here 6
days a week and then Libby in mornings…: I don't want to get worked again and pass
out like last time"* (05-08) — and the Libby money is earmarked in the messages
for specific purchases, most often phones and phone service.

**August — the break.** On **2024-08-06**: *"after I had gotten screamed at by
Libby you get mad over Amber taking me for ICECREAM."* Two days later the
household is a location rather than a person: *"Aka where Libby and Donald live
lol."* The work stops.

## The unpaid wages, and the letters Dan wrote

This is the part the first version of the page missed entirely, and it is the
most consequential thing on it.

Through August 2024 Annie was owed money, was **asked to sign an NDA**, and heard
nothing. **Dan drafted three escalating demand letters for her**, all of them
sent from his handle into the thread for her to use:

> **2024-08-01** — *"Dear x I'm reaching out to inform you of the unpaid wages
> which I have been unable to receive and request a date that I can be
> compensated. The total amount is x (y hours at **$75/hour**)…"*
>
> **2024-08-13, 00:18** — *"…I wanted to follow up with you about the unpaid wages
> that I had previously reached out to you about on (date of last email) as I had
> not received any response."*
>
> **2024-08-13, 01:00** — ***"Final Request for Payment of Unpaid Wages"***, with
> *"I would like to resolve this issue without any additional complications and am
> not interested in seeking further remedy from **Mr or Mrs Fagen**. Subsequently
> I have even agreed to sign…"*

Annie's own position on the NDA is stated once and it is a trade: *"As you know I
was asked to sign an NDA. which I have not heard anything about. And also put at
the end in exchange for signing an NDA I would like to receive the unpaid
wages"* (2024-08-01). She forwards the correspondence and the reply to Libby's
own address on 08-13, and on 08-14 adds the detail that fixes the rate: *"the
hourly rate was set by Libby Fagen."*

**The money was not abstract.** *"I may try to see if John will hold this weeks
rent check and explain to him the situation that I am waiting for a check from
Libby"* (2024-08-01) — [[wiki/people/john-paci|John]] being the landlord at
[[wiki/places/307-e-76th-st]].

**Nothing in the corpus records a resolution.** The last letter is 13 August. She
died on 13 October. On the evidence available the dispute was open when she died,
and this page will not assume otherwise in either direction.

> **This is the corpus's clearest instance of the forensic register turned
> outward on somebody else's behalf.** Dated correspondence, an itemised
> hours-times-rate total, an explicit statement of what remedy is *not* being
> sought, a final-notice escalation on a fixed interval — it is the same
> instrument [[wiki/mind/concepts/forensic-method]] describes him turning on his
> own relationships, and one of very few times in eleven years it is deployed for
> a third party's material benefit rather than to adjudicate a private grievance.
> Whether it worked is unknown. That he wrote it is not.

> **CONTRADICTION: the rate does not reconcile.** The demand letters state
> **$75/hour**, set by Libby. But on 2024-05-17 Annie writes *"I was literally
> with Libby for just over 3 hours today.. she paid me 500"* — roughly $167/hour —
> and a week later invites Dan to guess the figure for four hours. Both are
> first-hand and neither is retracted. Possible readings: the rate was raised or
> lowered between May and August; the $500 included back pay or a gift; or the
> $75 figure is the one Annie could evidence in writing and the cash payments were
> informal. **Unresolved, and recorded rather than smoothed.**

## What it corrects about Annie

**The standing account of Annie's employment is wrong for 2024.**
`raw/self/dox-md/Honest assessment and value judgment analysis.md` states she
*"was fired in 2023 and spent a full year unemployed,"* and the framing
propagated. She was working **two jobs** through the first half of 2024, at a
documented rate above anything on record for Dan in the same period, and when the
money stopped she pursued it formally. Corrected on [[wiki/people/annie-ulmer]].

The **$119K–$123K net outflow** at [[wiki/mind/synthesis/estate-money-spine]] is
unaffected — it is payment-app derived, not employment-derived — but the
single-earner reading of 2024 is not what the record supports, and the inbound
side of those exports has still never been swept.

## The texture, which is still worth keeping

The soured ending does not cancel what came before it, and the record of the
middle months is unusual for this archive: Annie is reliable, turns up, and is
trusted with money, medical appointments and correspondence by someone who
plainly liked her. It is also funny. Libby shows her a brooch and remarks *"I did
cocaine once, but I didn't like it"* (05-22). At an appointment she asks the woman
at the front desk where she can get her hat — it is a hijab — and on being told,
replies *"oh with my past I probably shouldn't"* (03-22). She fires her other
helper (05-02), takes against a replacement named Janine (05-10), gives Annie a
pair of loafers (05-09), and cc's her on so much correspondence that Annie ends up
looking at a spreadsheet of the household bank accounts and says she felt wrong
doing it (05-30).

Both things are true and the page holds them together: a woman dying of brain
cancer who liked the person helping her, and an employment relationship that
ended with a screaming match, an NDA, and three unanswered letters.

## Gaps

1. **Was the balance ever paid?** The last letter is 2024-08-13 and she died
   2024-10-13. Nothing in the corpus resolves it. The operator can answer in a
   sentence, and it is the last open fact about this relationship.
2. **How much was owed.** Every draft uses placeholders — *"The total amount is x
   (y hours at $75/hour)"*. The figure was never typed into the thread.
3. **The rate contradiction** above, unresolved.
4. **Was the NDA ever signed?** Raised twice in August, never mentioned again.
5. **The other 2024 job.** *"I'll be here 6 days a week"* names a second employer
   that appears nowhere in `wiki/work/` or on Annie's page. Still unidentified,
   and now the only part of her 2024 income the wiki cannot see at all.

# Libby
Libby was an elderly Manhattan woman for whom [[wiki/people/annie-ulmer|Annie]]
worked as a paid personal assistant and informal carer through **2024** — driving
her to hospital and doctor's appointments, taking her food, packing her
apartment, handling her correspondence, and being paid in cash and cheques at
rates that reached **$500 for a little over three hours**. Dan never met her. She
exists in this corpus entirely through Annie's running commentary, 116 messages
of it, and she is the single best-documented thing about Annie's working life in
the whole archive.
She matters here for three reasons that have nothing to do with her. She is the
**largest documented income source on Annie's side of the relationship**; she
falsifies a standing claim this wiki has carried about Annie's employment; and
the arrangement ends, along with the money, immediately before the period the
wiki dates as the collapse.
> **Sensitivity note.** This page concerns a private individual's health,
> finances and household, recorded from one side of a private conversation she
> was not party to and could not correct. It is kept because it is load-bearing
> for the biography of the person this wiki is about, and it is written to that
> standard and no further: what bears on Dan and Annie is here, and clinical
> detail beyond that is deliberately not. **This is a candidate for the portal
> seal** (`wiki.locks.json`, portal repo) and the operator should decide.
## The identification, and its evidential status
**Libby is very probably Libby Titus — born Elizabeth Jurist — the singer and
songwriter, married to Donald Fagen of Steely Dan.** The identification is
inferred rather than stated, and it rests on two independent things in the record
rather than on any outside search.
The first is Dan's own. On **2024-03-17 at 16:40** Annie writes *"Did you know
Libby was in a movie with Jack Nicholson"*, and at **22:33 that same evening** Dan
sends a link — five times, in the burst pattern the corpus is full of — to a
Tumblr post titled `girlfriend-muse-libby-titus-elizabeth-jurist`. He looked her
up the same night and filed the answer into the thread. That is a
contemporaneous identification made by the subject of this wiki, not a
reconstruction by it.
The second is corroboration from inside the household. Annie reports a **Donald**
who lives with Libby and who told her, on 2024-05-28, *"that he was the first
person to ever use the term 'gaslighting' in a song"* — at which *"Libby screamed
'YEAH ABOUT ME YOU ASSHOLE!'"* Steely Dan's *Gaslighting Abbie* is on **Two
Against Nature** (2000), and Fagen married Libby Titus in 1993. Two unrelated
details — a Jack Nicholson film credit and a spouse with that specific songwriting
claim — converge on one person.
**What the page does not do is treat this as verified.** No message names her
surname; the Tumblr link is Dan's inference from Annie's anecdote, and Annie
never confirms it. Recorded as **inferred identification with two supports**, and
flagged as such in the infobox.

**May onward — the money, and the second job.** The rate becomes explicit.

## What it corrects
**The standing account of Annie's employment is wrong for 2024.** The AI
assessment in `raw/self/dox-md/Honest assessment and value judgment analysis.md`
states that Annie *"was fired in 2023 and spent a full year unemployed"*, and the
framing has propagated. The message record shows her **working two jobs through
mid-2024** — a six-day-a-week position plus mornings at Libby's — and earning, at
the documented rate, more per hour than anything on record for Dan in the same
period. Corrected on [[wiki/people/annie-ulmer]].
This is not a small revision. The unemployment claim has been doing work in the
corpus's account of the relationship's economics, in which Dan is the sole
provider and the money runs one way
([[wiki/mind/synthesis/estate-money-spine]] records a net **$119K–$123K** outflow
from Dan to Annie across the decade). That total is unaffected — it is derived
from payment-app records, not from an employment assumption — but the picture of
2024 specifically is not what the wiki has been carrying.
## The texture, which is the part worth keeping
Almost nothing in this corpus records Annie doing something for somebody else
over a sustained period, without an audience, and the Libby material is the
largest such stretch in eleven years. It is also, unusually for this archive,
funny. Libby shows her a brooch and remarks *"I did cocaine once, but I didn't
like it"* (05-22). At a medical appointment she asks the woman at the front desk
where she can get her hat — it is a hijab — and on being told, replies *"oh with
my past I probably shouldn't"* (03-22). She fires her other helper (05-02), takes
against a replacement named Janine (05-10), gives Annie a pair of loafers (05-09),
and cc's her on so much correspondence that Annie ends up looking at a spreadsheet
of the household bank accounts and says she felt wrong doing it (05-30).
Annie's own register in these messages is worth noting against the rest of her
record: she is reliable, she turns up, she is trusted with money, medical
appointments and correspondence, and the person she is working for likes her.
None of that appears anywhere else in the corpus at this length.
1. **When and how it ended.** 115 messages in 2024, one in 2025, and no closing
event anywhere. Did Libby die, move, or simply stop calling? The operator can
almost certainly answer in a sentence, and it dates the start of Annie's
income collapse.
2. **What the total came to.** Individual payments are visible ($500 for three
hours; an unstated figure for four) but no running total exists. The Venmo and
Cash App records that establish the Dan→Annie flow would show the other
direction if they were swept for it.
3. **Whether the identification is right.** One sentence from the operator —
he sent the Tumblr link — settles it. If wrong, the two supports above need
another explanation and this page needs a correction rather than an edit.
4. **The other job.** *"I'll be here 6 days a week"* names a second 2024 employer
that appears nowhere in `wiki/work/` or on Annie's page. Unidentified.
